summary.suggested: The St. Louis Post-Dispatch reported that Judge Noonan released Tom Allen rather than hold him for Kentucky over his 1876 prize fight with Joe Goss, finding the case was an attempt by his bondsman Farrell to collect a debt.

facts.fact: Allen fought Joe Goss in 1876 on the Kentucky side of the river near Covington; the whole party was arrested
After the Goss fight Allen took a steamer to England and took up his residence there, while Goss returned to Kentucky, stood trial and was fined $300
On returning to America Allen came to St. Louis, where trouble over his forfeited Kentucky bond began
Allen was arrested in St. Louis at the instance of his former bondsman Farrell to await a requisition from Kentucky

At a hearing in the Court of Criminal Correction, the defense said the case was an attempt by Farrell to collect a debt; the prosecutor declined to press it and Judge Noonan released Allen from custody
places: Court of Criminal Correction, St. Louis
